bodyMarkdown:
## Actuary Salary Sydney: Understanding Your Pay

If you are researching an **actuary salary Sydney** offer or want to compare your current hourly rate, it helps to break down the numbers across different pay periods. This guide explains how to convert an hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, and how tax, super, and casual loading affect your take-home amount.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. For a full-time employee, the standard week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. For example, if your hourly rate is $50, your annual gross pay is $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800. Weekly pay is $50 × 38 = $1,900, and fortnightly pay is $1,900 × 2 = $3,800.

This formula assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for budgeting and comparing offers.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, according to the Fair Work Commission. This is the base rate for award/agreement-free adult employees. Most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides with minimum rates for each award, which increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026. An actuary in Sydney is likely covered by a professional or industry award, or an enterprise agreement, so your rate will be above the minimum.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate, as specified in the National Minimum Wage Order. On [the timesheet](/), you enter your base hourly rate and check a box to add the 25% loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading. For example, a base rate of $30 becomes $37.50 per hour casual. The loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation is an additional cost paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your salary; it is paid into a super fund separately. For an annual gross salary of $98,800, the super contribution would be $11,856 (12% of $98,800), bringing the total employment cost to $110,656. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains more about salary sacrifice and contribution caps.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Income tax for 2026–27 residents uses the following brackets:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The tax and Medicare estimates on this site use the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. For a single person earning $98,800, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be around $22,000 – $23,000, depending on offsets. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a detailed breakdown.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For a $50/hour rate, that is $3,800 gross per fortnight. After tax and Medicare, your net pay will be lower. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool can help you switch between periods.

### Actuary Salary Sydney: What the Data Shows

While the search results did not provide a specific actuary salary figure for Sydney, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult employees at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). Actuaries typically earn above this average due to their specialised skills and qualifications. For precise market rates, consult industry salary surveys, job advertisements, or professional bodies like the Actuaries Institute. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page has more context on earnings across occupations.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

The [timesheet](/), our home page, is the simplest way to convert your hourly rate. Enter your base hourly rate, select whether you are casual (adds 25% loading), and the calculator shows your weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and annual gross pay. It also estimates tax and super. Remember that super is paid on top, not deducted. The results are estimates only and should be verified with your employer or a tax professional.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For award-specific rates, check the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman or use the PACT calculator to find your award. The [reference tables](/data) on this site provide historical rates and comparisons.

Whether you are negotiating an **actuary salary Sydney** offer or planning your budget, understanding these components helps you make informed decisions. Start with your hourly rate, add casual loading if applicable, and remember that super is an extra benefit paid by your employer.
